title: Boilerplate Launchpad: Quickstart visuals, annotated screenshots, README diagrams
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create a cohesive set of onboarding assets for the Boilerplate Launchpad reference app used in the docs quickstart and README. Assets include annotated screenshots (first-run, API key setup, console dashboard), a two-panel architecture SVG for README, a compact flow diagram for the quickstart page, and exported image variants (2x PNGs, WebP, and optimized SVG). Aim is to reduce first-time setup friction and make the reference app screenshots deterministic and easy to update across releases.
background_and_goals: The current reference app screenshots are inconsistent across docs and the READMEs are missing clear visuals for Dedicated and Private deployment flows. This ticket produces a single source-of-truth visual pack (screenshots + diagrams) that docs, solutions engineering, and the onboarding templates can reuse. Goals: 1) lower time-to-first-success for new users; 2) reduce doc churn when UI/console surface changes; 3) provide retina-ready assets for marketing/devrel snippets.
acceptance_criteria: All screenshots captured from the canonical reference app running on staging (stable seed data) with deterministic timestamps and masked PII.
Annotated screenshots exported in PNG@2x, WebP, and an SVG overlay for key callouts.
Two README diagrams: (a) minimal onboarding flow for README top-of-file; (b) architecture diagram showing Hosted/Dedicated/Private routing for the quickstart docs.
Assets uploaded to the shared Drive folder and linked in the PR and Confluence spec.
Docs team confirmed they can swap images into quickstart in one pass; engineering reviewed for accuracy.
PR created updating reference app README with new images and diagrams; at least one PM and one ENG approval on the PR.
work_items: 1) Run reference app on staging with deterministic seed and capture 1920x1080 screenshots
2) Mask API keys and user emails using screenshot pipeline script
3) Create annotated overlays in Figma, add pointer labels and short copy (8-10 words each)
4) Export PNG@2x, WebP, and SVG callouts; generate small web-optimized versions
5) Produce README top-of-file 2-panel flow (Get API key + First API call) as SVG
6) Add architecture diagram for quickstart docs showing routing choices and where to change model pinning
7) Upload all assets to Drive and update docs PR and Confluence spec
8) Gather feedback from Docs, PM, and ENG and iterate (collect sign-offs)
risks_and_tradeoffs: To keep screenshots stable we seed staging with mock data and freeze UI state; this risks showing slightly outdated console chrome if UI changes before next release. Tradeoff chosen: freeze visuals now (release-2026.03) and add a lightweight visual-check job to the docs PR process for future updates instead of blocking the release on a design freeze.
decisions: Use staging environment with seeded data for deterministic screenshots (decision logged 2026-02-15).
Export PNG@2x and WebP for web pages; keep a single SVG source for diagrams and overlays so docs can recolor as needed (decision 2026-02-18).
